issues.legal_issue: A reliable sale of land in the same village may be preferred to later sales from another village or sales of small plots when assessing compensation for acquired land.
material_facts: The acquired lands were agricultural lands in one village.
A sale deed concerned agricultural land in the same village and was the only sale exemplar from that village.
The other sale deeds relied on by the claimants concerned land in another village and were either later than the acquisition or related to small areas.
issues.conclusion: The court upheld the use of the same-village sale deed as the appropriate exemplar for determining the market value of the acquired lands.
issues.legal_principle: Market value may be assessed using a relevant sale exemplar, and the same-village exemplar was preferable on these facts to later sales or sales of small plots in another village. The proceedings involved references under Section 34 of the Maharashtra Industrial Development Act, 1961, read with Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and same_village_sale_exemplar and (other_village_sales_are_later or other_sales_involve_small_plots)

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the amount of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.same_village_sale_exemplar: A sale of land in the same village as the acquired land is available as a market-value exemplar.
predicates.other_village_sales_are_later: The competing sale evidence from another village relates to sales later than the acquisition.
predicates.other_sales_involve_small_plots: The competing sale evidence relates to small plots rather than land comparable in scale to the acquired land.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal involves a same-village sale exemplar and the competing other-village sales are later or concern small plots, the same-village sale may be used as the best comparator.

issues.legal_issue: A cumulative annual increase of 12 percent was appropriate to account for the interval between the comparable sale and the acquisition.
material_facts: The comparable sale took place about three years before the acquisition.
The High Court had applied a cumulative annual increase of 10 percent.
The court considered that a cumulative increase in the range of 10 to 15 percent could be accepted and found 12 percent appropriate on these facts.
issues.conclusion: The court modified the valuation by applying a cumulative annual increase of 12 percent instead of 10 percent.
issues.legal_principle: A cumulative increase of 10 to 15 percent per year may be accepted depending on the facts; the court relied on Pehlad Ram v. Haryana Urban Development Authority, (2014) 14 SCC 778.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and comparable_sale_precedes_acquisition and valuation_used_lower_cumulative_increase and case_supports_higher_increase

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the amount of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.comparable_sale_precedes_acquisition: The comparable sale occurred before the acquisition and there is a time interval to account for.
predicates.valuation_used_lower_cumulative_increase: The valuation under appeal applied a cumulative increase that the reviewing court found too low.
predicates.case_supports_higher_increase: The circumstances support a higher cumulative increase within the range accepted by the court.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns a prior comparable sale and the lower increase used in the valuation is inadequate on the circumstances, the valuation must use the cumulative increase found just on those circumstances.

issues.legal_issue: The intended industrial or commercial use of acquired agricultural land does not, by itself, justify increasing its market value, though its inherent non-agricultural potential may be relevant.
material_facts: The acquired lands were agricultural when acquired.
The land was acquired for extending an industrial estate and was intended for industrial use.
Development expenditure would be required for industrial use, but development charges had not been deducted in the valuation under review.
The court separately recognized the lands’ non-agricultural potential and location when adjusting compensation.
issues.conclusion: The intended use or purpose of acquisition could not itself be used to increase market value; the court nevertheless accounted for the lands’ non-agricultural potential in the valuation.
issues.legal_principle: The owner is compensated for what was lost, not by reference to the purpose of acquisition; that purpose cannot itself increase market value. The court relied on Hookiyar Singh v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, (1996) 3 SCC 766, and explained the qualification to the discussion in Subh Ram v. State of Haryana, (2010) 1 SCC 444. Development expenditure is relevant to determining compensation, while inherent potentiality may also be considered.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the amount of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.agricultural_land_at_acquisition: The land was agricultural when it was acquired.
predicates.industrial_or_commercial_future_use: The acquiring body intended to use the land for industrial or commercial purposes.

issues.definition: If agricultural land is acquired for intended industrial or commercial use, that future use alone does not increase its market value.

issues.legal_issue: Different compensation rates may be justified for lands in the same village when their locations or qualities differ.
material_facts: The acquired lands were in the same village but were located differently.
The High Court had assigned different compensation rates to the lands, taking their locations into account.
issues.conclusion: The court held that different compensation rates for lands in the same village were permissible where the lands differed in location or quality.
issues.legal_principle: Lands within one village need not have the same market value; location and potentiality can affect value. The court relied on Tarlochan Singh v. State of Punjab, (1995) 2 SCC 424, Basant Kumar, and Kanwar Singh v. Union of India, (1998) 8 SCC 136.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the amount of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.lands_share_a_village: The acquired lands are situated within the same village.
predicates.lands_differ_in_location_or_quality: The lands differ in location, quality, or potentiality in a way that affects their market value.

issues.definition: When acquired lands in the same village differ in location or quality, different compensation rates may be set for them.

issues.legal_issue: Interest on enhanced compensation may be withheld for the period of delay in filing the relevant appeals.
material_facts: Two of the claimants’ appeals were filed after delays of 613 days and 438 days.
The court directed that those claimants would not receive interest on the enhanced compensation for the respective delayed periods.
issues.conclusion: The claimants in the delayed appeals were not entitled to interest on the enhanced compensation for the periods of delay in filing their appeals.
issues.legal_principle: The court made a case-specific direction limiting interest on enhanced compensation to exclude the periods of delay in filing the appeals.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the amount of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.appeal_filed_after_delay: The claimant filed the appeal after a period of delay.
predicates.enhanced_compensation_awarded: The claimant obtained an award of compensation higher than the earlier award.

issues.definition: When a claimant obtains enhanced compensation in an appeal filed after delay, interest on that enhancement is excluded for the period of delay.
